subject: Request: temporary queueing carveout & reserved GPU behavior — NarrowBand launch
messages:
From: Emily Ng <emily.ng@narrowband.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: jordan.lee@narrowband.ai, procure@narrowsupplies.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production launch — temporary carveout for reserved GPUs / queue behavior

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the Dedicated pool is looking good. We have a product launch on Sept 8 and expect a two-week spike in low-latency web inference traffic driven by many concurrent short prompts (avg tokens ~40). Our SRE lead (Jordan) asked whether Redwood can temporarily relax queue depth preemption on our reserved GPU pool so customer-facing short requests don't get batched into long-running jobs during the launch window.

Specific asks:
- A carveout window 2026-09-08 00:00 - 2026-09-22 23:59 PDT where preemption for nightly batch workloads is delayed by up to 45 minutes for our pool.
- A soft throughput guarantee: 95th percentile tokens/sec for short inference traffic not to drop below 70% of baseline.
- We can accept usage credits if the carveout impacts other tenants, and we attached our expected hourly traffic profile.

Can Redwood provide an SLA addendum or temporary amendment for this? If needed we can sign a one-off addendum and share SOC evidence.

Thanks,
Emily Ng
Head of SRE — NarrowBand Systems
emily.ng@narrowband.ai

Attachment: traffic_profile_q3.csv (csv)

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ng <emily.ng@narrowband.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production launch — temporary carveout for reserved GPUs / queue behavior

Emily,

Appreciate the heads-up and the dataset — this is the right time to plan. Short answer: we can offer a time-bound carveout but we need to align on three operational guards so we don't jeopardize other tenants' SLOs. High-level proposal follows.

Proposed temporary addendum (summary):
1) Window: 2026-09-08 07:00 UTC - 2026-09-22 07:00 UTC (matches your PDT window).
2) Preemption delay: defer eviction of short-token web requests from your reserved nodes for up to 45 minutes. During deferment we will: 
   - Enforce strict prefix caching for repeated prompts,
   - Cap long-batch admission when your pool is >85% occupied.
3) Throughput measurement: 95th pct tokens/sec measured on your model route(s) against baseline week (we'll use 2026-08-24—30). If throughput falls below 70% for >2 hours, we trigger an automated mitigation (burst capacity from Dedicated burst pool or temporary routing to a compatible quantized variant).
4) Credits: If mitigation cannot restore 70% within 2 hours and we miss the temporary SLO for >4 cumulative hours, Redwood will apply a pro-rated usage credit (formula in attached addendum draft).

Next steps: I need legal to prepare a short addendum and Product to confirm runtime gating knobs. Ben — can you start an internal ops ticket so we can attach the runbook and measurement dashboard? Lauren — can you confirm if the Dedicated burst pool has the headroom required for this window?

I'll loop Naomi (CS) if we need a customer-facing runbook. Emily, Jordan — if that's acceptable I'll circulate a one-page addendum and a runbook for sign-off by Wed 02 Sep.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

Attachment: narrowband_sla_addendum_v1.pdf (draft)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Production launch — temporary carveout for reserved GPUs / queue behavior

Rafael / Lauren — quick ops notes: 
- Burst pool: We have an elastic burst pool that can provide up to ~25% additional token throughput for short-window events in us-west (subject to other commitments). We need to reserve those nodes by 2026-09-04 to guarantee placement.
- Queue gating: We can implement the "cap long-batch admission" knob by model route ID; it will require a config push and a monitoring threshold. Ops estimates ~10 engineer-hours to implement and validate.
- Measurement: Recommend we measure baseline on tokens/sec per route and tail latency (p99) with a rolling 1-hour window.

If Rafael confirms, I'll open the infra ticket and schedule the config change for 09/06 PST dry-run.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Emily Ng <emily.ng@narrowband.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: jordan.lee@narrowband.ai, procure@narrowsupplies.com
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production launch — temporary carveout for reserved GPUs / queue behavior

Thanks Rafael — that approach sounds reasonable. A couple clarifications before we sign:
1) Can the preemption delay be scoped per route (we only want web-inference routes deferred, not nightly retrain pipelines)?
2) For the mitigation step, can you confirm whether routing to a "compatible quantized variant" changes model outputs deterministically (does quality drift require regression checks)? We can accept brief output variance but need to know risk levels.

Jordan (SRE) and I reviewed your timing; we'll be ready to sign the one-page addendum if the scoping and mitigation details are explicit. Please cc ProcureOps once the formal DOC is ready.

Emily

On Tue, Sep 1, 2026 at 11:17 AM Emily Ng <emily.ng@narrowband.ai> wrote:
> FYI attached the traffic profile.

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ng <emily.ng@narrowband.ai>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 21:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production launch — temporary carveout for reserved GPUs / queue behavior

Emily / Jordan — looping back with the team confirmation and scope language for the addendum. Apologies for the terse note — we wanted to be explicit.

Final proposed scoping (to include in the one-page addendum):
- Route scoping: The preemption delay will only apply to model routes listed in Appendix A (web-inference routes). Nightly batch and retrain pipelines are explicitly excluded.
- Quality & mitigation: The quantized variant is a model variant we have validated for parity on your typical prompt set (baseline regression tests pass within agreed tolerance). Any fallback routing will be flagged in the incident channel and we will run a short regression job for the next 6 hours. If regression exceeds tolerance, Redwood will revert routing and apply credits as per the addendum.
- Reservation and dry-run: Ben will reserve burst capacity and schedule a dry-run on 2026-09-06 PST; narrowband team to provide 30-min synthetic traffic window for validation.
- Signatures: ProcureOps (procure@narrowsupplies.com) will receive the DocuSign link for the addendum.

I'll send the formal addendum (one page + Appendix A) by EOD Fri 03 Sep for legal and ProcureOps signatures. Naomi will own the customer runbook and on-call escalation.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: narrowband_sla_addendum_v1.pdf (updated)
